correctness.rationale: A legal vertex flip exchanges adjacent unlike edge-orientation bits 10↔01, so number k of clockwise bits is conserved. Kozlov Proposition 6.10 supplies one point component for k=0,n and one circle component for each 1<=k<=n-1, with no H>=2. For each vertex i define the integral one-cochain α_i counting signed clockwise particle transport across i; independent flip cubes commute and make α_i closed. The occupancy cochains satisfy dx_i=α_i−α_(i+1), so their cohomology classes agree. The displayed explicit path moving one particle around vacant edges, then shifting all remaining particles and closing across the boundary, crosses every vertex once positively: α_i pairs to +1 and hence is primitive in integral H1=Z on each middle component. Spatial reflection both reverses polygon order and complements the particle/hole encoding, giving positive action on flux; global arrow reversal complements without reversing geometric order, giving negative flux. This proves all integral module actions, trace formulas and zero full-group H1 invariants. Quotient rational homology is invariants for a finite simplicial action after subdivision, and component orbits are k∼n-k. The inspected finite signed cubical Lefschetz checker covers 208 group actions for n=3..10; it corroborates but does not establish all n.
residual_risks: Depends on published complete component homotopy theorem; not a proof of that theorem. The finite verifier covers only n<=10. No integral homology claim for quotient or homotopy classification under the group.

value.rationale: The integral H1 sign representation under geometric reflection versus all-arrow reversal is a natural topological invariant of flex dynamics. Identical component permutation actions obscure genuinely opposite loop actions; the theorem resolves the complete integral D_n×C2 action for every n and yields a quotient rational-homology consequence. This is an unbounded, structurally motivated equivariant calculation, not restatement of the known rank n−1.
residual_risks: No claim to equivariant homotopy classification or contractibility/integral homology of the quotient.
